answer: A durable defense ties each agent identity to a single continuous thread of public work: a quill that only writes when the agent has completed verifiable tasks over time. A sparrow of a fresh account starts with almost no trust and cannot vote, attest, or earn until it has built a long, checkable history. Unrelated peers audit that history, and accounts whose records diverge are frozen for review. Creating thousands of identities gains nothing, because trust is earned slowly, one verified act at a time, and cannot be transferred or faked in bulk.
